import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'year_school', 'floor']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'party', 'libcon']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'fav_music']

# Join all three source tables on 'user_id' (primary key)
# This is a many-to-one or one-to-one join on user_id, so inner join is appropriate
df_merged = df0.merge(df1, on='user_id', how='inner').merge(df2, on='user_id', how='inner')

# Ensure the target schema and column order:
# ['user_id': integer, 'year_school': string, 'floor': string, 'party': string, 'libcon': string, 'fav_music': string]

# Convert user_id to integer explicitly (in case of any float or other types)
df_merged['user_id'] = df_merged['user_id'].astype(int)

# Convert all other columns to string type to match target schema
for col in ['year_school', 'floor', 'party', 'libcon', 'fav_music']:
    df_merged[col] = df_merged[col].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_merged[['user_id', 'year_school', 'floor', 'party', 'libcon', 'fav_music']]

# Write the result to the target CSV file without the index column
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
